results.title: TGIIC proposes 27,500 acres for Telangana industries
results.description: Telangana : Telangana is planning large-scale land acquisition across the state to facilitate industrial development, with the process having begun in 22 districts. The Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) proposed the acquisition of more than 27,500 acres to the revenue department between December 2023 and June 2026. During the same period, it acquired more than […] Telangana : Telangana is planning large-scale land acquisition across the state to facilitate industrial development, with the process having begun in 22 districts. The Telangana Industrial Infrastructure Corporation (TGIIC) proposed the acquisition of more than 27,500 acres to the revenue department between December 2023 and June 2026. During the same period, it acquired more than 8,080 acres. Hyderabad region sees strong demand for industrial land Demand for industrial land has risen sharply in areas around Hyderabad. Despite high land prices, manufacturing, e-commerce and technology companies are competing for space in these locations. Investments are also coming from companies supplying components to defence and aerospace firms, besides those in pharmaceuticals, plastics and fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG). E-commerce companies are setting up large warehouses, while major firms are lining up to establish data centres. As a result, TGIIC is focusing on acquiring larger parcels in districts surrounding Hyderabad and those close to the state capital. The corporation is acquiring more than 10,000 acres in Vikarabad and Rangareddy districts alone, indicating the demand for land in the region. TGIIC hands over 2,400 acres to companies Between December 2023 and June 2026, more than 1,140 companies came forward to set up industries in Telangana. Together, they proposed investments of more than ₹94,000 crore. TGIIC handed over 2,400 acres to these companies. The firms that received land from the government have proposed creating employment for 85,000 people as part of their investment plans. Rangareddy district topped the list in industrial investments, followed by Nalgonda, Sangareddy, Medchal and Bhadradri Kothagudem. The pharmaceuticals and chemicals sectors attracted the highest investments, followed by solar and other renewable energy, industrial parks, IT buildings, food processing and engineering. District-wise land acquisition proposals District Proposed Acquired Vikarabad 5,051 acres 1,819 acres Rangareddy 5,011 acres 1,771 acres Sangareddy 4,161 acres 2,708 acres Medak 3,331 acres 137 acres Medchal-Malkajgiri 2,316 acres 428 acres Adilabad 2,062 acres — Nalgonda 818 acres — Narayanpet 562 acres — Mahabubnagar 416 acres — Yadadri Bhuvanagiri 344 acres — Average investment per unit rises nearly threefold The state received investment proposals worth ₹10,237 crore in the previous financial year. Between April and September this year, the government approved proposals worth ₹16,384 crore. A total of 1,172 industrial units have been approved so far this year, with the projects expected to create 30,511 jobs. In 2025-26, 2,163 units received the green light, with 51,029 jobs expected to be created. The average investment per unit rose from ₹4.7 crore last year to about ₹13.9 crore this year, nearly three times the previous figure. The Telangana government has also received another 1,178 proposals involving total investments of ₹79,032 crore. These proposals are yet to receive government approval and could create 87,863 jobs. ]]>
